verdict.line: You lose if you let her land E before her Q is up and get chain-dashed into a kill; you win if you farm mini-Gnar's range advantage into a Mega Gnar who out-skirmishes her with R.

brief.thesis: Irelia's kit exists to close the exact distance Gnar's kit exists to hold: her E (Flawless Duet) converges two blades to stun and Mark you, which lets her Q (Bladesurge) dash in for free, heal, and refresh its own cooldown if it kills a minion on the way out. Mini Gnar's 1100-range Q (Boomerang Throw) and Hyper-stacked autos want to poke from outside that 600-range Q leash, not trade inside it. The matchup swings entirely on whether you let her land E first or force her to approach into your boomerang.

theirWindow.when: Her E lands and marks you
theirWindow.what: A landed E (Flawless Duet) stuns and Marks you, and a Marked target refreshes her Q (Bladesurge) on hit — she will dash in immediately for the stun-into-Q combo, healing off it. If she's also stacked Conqueror and Ionian Fervor attack speed, this is her all-in window; disengage rather than trade through it.

yourWindow.what: With Q down she has no gap closer, so mini Gnar's 1100-range Q and Hyper-boosted autos can poke freely from max range. Walk up, throw Q (Boomerang Throw) for the slow, and back off before she closes the distance on cooldown reset.

start.why: The 57% pick rate option (51.1% WR, 180 games) gives sustain through poke trades and early AD to make Boomerang Throw hurt before you have any real item power.

boots.why: 95.4% pick for a reason — Irelia's whole kit is auto-attack and on-hit resets through Ionian Fervor stacks, and flat physical damage reduction blunts that far more than Mercury's Treads' tenacity.

core.why: The dominant core path (65.5% WR over 29 games with this build order) gives the burst, move speed, and on-hit damage mini and Mega Gnar both need to actually punish her approach.
Armor shred stacks fastest through Hyper-boosted autos and makes her Defiant Dance's damage reduction window less safe for her to sit in.
Tenacity and the health/AD spike let you survive the E-stun-into-Q all-in instead of getting deleted in it.

situational.when: she's snowballing on attack speed and you need the active slow to stop her from closing Q range
her Q heal and Ionian Fervor sustain are keeping her alive through every trade
you're getting run down early and need the grievous wounds and armor before Cleaver completes

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain and move speed burst reward exactly the poke-and-retreat pattern this lane demands — you're dodging her engage, not standing in melee range. Master-tier players run Lethal Tempo instead (1,985 games); that fits players who plan to win trades by sustaining attack speed in extended skirmishes rather than disengaging, which is riskier against her Q-refresh pattern.

summoners.why: The top combo at 51.9% WR and 52.1% pick rate — Flash to dodge the E-stun-into-Q combo, Teleport to reset onto the wave after you've been forced off it by her pressure, since this is a defensive matchup where you're conceding lane tempo.

playing.title: Bait her Q onto minions, not you
playing.detail: If she dashes a Bladesurge into a minion and kills it, the cooldown refreshes — don't let her get a free reset off creep while you're in range to be the next target.

playing.title: Never stand still after her E
playing.detail: A landed E (Flawless Duet) Marks you for 850 range and sets up a guaranteed Q follow-up with lifesteal attached; walk out of the stun's effective range the instant you see the blades converge, not after.

playing.title: Transform to Mega Gnar before you engage, not during
playing.detail: Mega Gnar's E (Crunch) and W (Wallop) are area tools that trade far better into her melee kit than mini Gnar's mobility tools do — bait Rage up with safe pokes, then commit the transform on your terms.

playing.title: Hold R for her Defiant Dance window
playing.detail: GNAR! slows and can stun her against a wall; use it to punish the W (Defiant Dance) charge-up window when she's committed to a big hit and can't reposition.

playing.title: Deny CS instead of trading in melee
playing.detail: With lane and solo-kill advantage on her side per the data, your goal through levels 3-6 is farming from range with Boomerang Throw, not matching her in straight trades.

playing.title: Watch her passive stacks before any skirmish
playing.detail: Ionian Fervor gives her bonus attack speed and, at max stacks, bonus on-hit damage — if she's been spell-weaving on minions or you, her next few autos hit much harder than they look.

playing.title: Itemize into her sustain, not just her burst
playing.detail: Her Q heal and passive attack speed mean straight damage trades favor her over time; Thornmail or Bramble Vest flip that math if she's outscaling you on sustain alone.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG game data on the current patch (16.20.1) — win rates, pick rates, and sample sizes are factual. The trade-pattern and timing analysis layered on top is my own tactical reading of the ability kits, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful when she has 5 (P) and Conqueror stacks. Avoid being hit with her (E) while kiting her. Use [R] to try to kill her.
